title: Write jmap-chat-federation-guide.md companion implementer guide
description:
Companion implementer guide for draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00, covering the operational and policy topics the federation draft defers to deployments.

CONTEXT

The federation draft (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md, ~690 lines) defines the Peer/* method set, peer discovery via /.well-known/jmap, identity binding, outbox semantics, retry/backoff, blocked-sender handling, and so on. Some federation-relevant deployment topics are already covered in jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md (Section 4 'Storage and retention' covers outbox durability mechanism and federation cache TTLs; Section 5.4 covers retry/backoff intervals; Section 6.3 covers blocked-sender ephemeral-event suppression). What is NOT covered there is the operational-system view of federation: how a deployment actually federates with other deployments.

SCOPE (proposed)

Seven sections, each in the established 'what spec leaves open + what to decide + considerations + common patterns + recommended starting point' shape:

1. Peer authentication mechanism choice
   - Spec permits mTLS, OAuth client-credentials, bearer tokens (out-of-band enrollment), overlay-network membership (e.g. Tailscale).
   - Each has different rotation, revocation, and operational profiles.
   - Tradeoffs and recommended defaults for common deployment contexts.

2. Federation allowlist / denylist policy
   - Open federation vs invite-only vs corporate-trust-domain models.
   - How to express the policy (config files, admin UI, runtime API).
   - Onboarding and offboarding peers.

3. /.well-known/jmap discovery hygiene
   - Caching strategy and refresh triggers (per the federation draft's deferral on cache TTL via uy1m.3).
   - Handling of unreachable peers (transient vs persistent failure).
   - Pre-cache warming on known peers.

4. Onboarding a new peer
   - First-contact workflow.
   - Identity binding verification (the spec's authentication-vs-discovery correspondence check).
   - Capability negotiation: which Peer/* methods to expect, which extensions to advertise.

5. Hostile-peer detection and mitigation
   - Rate-limiting per peer (the spec already requires this for Peer/typing; what about Peer/deliver?).
   - Abuse-signal aggregation across multiple peers.
   - Defederation procedures (graceful vs emergency).
   - Quarantine vs full defederation.

6. Cross-server moderation
   - What happens when a federated peer's user misbehaves in a local Space.
   - Local block of remote ChatContact (already spec'd; cover UX patterns).
   - Peer abuse reports (out-of-band; suggest reporting formats and workflows).
   - Defederation as escalation step.

7. Federation observability
   - Logging Peer/* method calls and responses.
   - Metrics to expose (delivery success rate, retry depth, peer round-trip time, queue depth).
   - Distinguishing peer-down from local-bug.
   - Dashboards and alerting patterns.

(Possible additional section: Federation testing and certification. Out of scope for v0 unless demand surfaces.)

WHAT THIS GUIDE DOES NOT NEED TO COVER

- Outbox durability mechanism: already in implementer guide §4.1.
- Edit-history retention: in implementer guide §4.2.
- Cache TTL specifics: in implementer guide §4.3.
- Retry/backoff intervals: in implementer guide §5.4.
- Blocked-sender ephemeral-event suppression: in implementer guide §6.3.
- The protocol itself: in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md.

WORK PLAN

Similar to fo22 (the implementer guide epic):
1. Skeleton with all section headings and stubs (single commit).
2. Fill in sections 1-7 in order; commit per major section.
3. Cross-reference into the implementer guide where topics overlap.
4. Final pass for consistency.

The 'A note on RFC 2119 keywords' wrapper at the top is mandatory (per the convention established in commit 21a4bb6).

P4: not urgent. Federation deployments are still rare; this guide is parked aspirational. Promote priority when demand materializes.
acceptance_criteria:
- jmap-chat-federation-guide.md exists at the top level of the repo.
- All seven proposed top-level sections (or a defensibly-revised set) are present and non-empty.
- Each topic section follows the established shape (what spec leaves open + what to decide + considerations + common patterns + recommended starting point).
- 'A note on RFC 2119 keywords' wrapper at top.
- No content duplicated from jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md; instead cross-referenced.
- Cross-reference table at the bottom links to spec, main implementer guide, and any related guides.
- AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended to include federation-guide topics.
- Implementer-guide cross-reference table extended to include federation-guide.
close_reason: Both companion guides written: jmap-chat-federation-guide.md (850 lines, 7 sections) and jmap-chat-filenode-guide.md (937 lines, 8 sections). Each section follows the established 5-subsection pattern. RFC 2119 wrapper present in both. Cross-reference tables added at the bottom of each guide. AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended. jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md cross-ref table extended.
